parallel.requirements: Parallel recognized the clean-room task, CLI compatibility, archive password search, dictionary mode, brute-force mode, file selection, and ZipCrypto/AES support.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent fanned out docs, fixture, runtime, and review work while also owning the final implementation; children drifted into implementation and build ownership in the same workspace.
parallel.implementation: The final delivered path became a Go implementation with manual CLI parsing, zip target loading, password testing, worker search, and a compile.sh build script.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration involved reconciling live child writes, unexpected Rust Cargo/src files, overlapping Go files, and build-script changes before final delivery.
parallel.verification: Parallel ran local build, vet, compile, and fixture checks across bundled archives and representative error paths before final response.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed with 42 failures, and the trajectory shows unstable final-tree provenance from concurrent deliverable writes even though the final response reported success.

serial.requirements: Serial recognized the same clean-room task and key CLI/search/archive obligations, including help/version text, validation errors, dictionary, brute force, startingPassword, fileNumber, ZipCrypto, and AES.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Serial kept a single owner for probing, implementation, build-script updates, verification, and final delivery rather than delegating any source or build path.
serial.implementation: Serial wrote a standalone Go implementation split across main.go, search.go, and zipcheck.go, initialized go.mod, and adjusted compile.sh to rebuild executable.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Serial used one coherent Go source tree and fixed the build script to remove the original executable before producing the final binary.
serial.verification: Serial ran final build and representative fixture/error checks, then reported the remaining empty-charset panic compatibility risk.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed with 25 failures, so serial was materially stronger but not a passing solution.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel understood it needed a clean-room replacement executable based on observed behavior and bundled documentation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked from the same prompt and pursued the same clean-room behavioral replacement objective.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-detection difference is proven; the difference appears later in shared-state handling and final implementation coherence.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spawned multiple children for docs and fixture probing while the parent also kept final implementation ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial followed one self-contained plan from behavioral model through Go implementation and final build.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's decomposition created overlapping implementation/build ownership, while serial kept ownership centralized and sequential.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children had enough task context to produce implementations, but no stable workspace/file ownership boundary kept their build products separate.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no cross-agent context transfer or interface boundary; the same agent carried observations into implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material interface issue was not a missing task brief but a shared deliverable workspace where agents wrote incompatible or superseding files.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel saw both a Rust scaffold from one child and overlapping Go source from parent/child activity before delivering Go.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote Go source and build files in one implementation path without a competing language scaffold.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had competing implementation artifacts to reconcile; serial stayed with one Go codebase and therefore had less integration churn.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children produced usable observations and code artifacts, but their file results appeared directly in the live worktree instead of as isolated handoffs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child lifecycle to join; intermediate findings stayed local and were directly incorporated into the evolving implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The adverse lifecycle boundary was not an unjoined result; it was that parallel results materialized as live file writes requiring later reconciliation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel agents wrote or superseded build and entrypoint artifacts in the same workspace, and later actors detected changed compile.sh, overlapping Go files, and unexpected Rust files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial edited compile.sh once to remove the original executable and then built the final Go binary successfully from the coherent tree.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the concrete task-solving difference: parallel spent integration effort cleaning and reconciling live shared-state writes; serial maintained a stable deliverable path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel reported local build, vet, compile, and fixture verification before final delivery, but official evaluation still failed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also verified bundled fixtures and representative errors, explicitly noting one residual empty-charset panic risk before final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both verified locally and both failed officially; serial's verification was attached to a cleaner source/build path and a higher score.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used five subagents and many more tool calls/tokens, then closed after cleanup and final checks without timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, fewer requests and tool calls, and closed after final build and checks without timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had coordination overhead and shared-state cleanup, but the official relation is still both_fail rather than a discordant timeout or pass/fail difference.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are not discordant: parallel failed with 749/792 and serial failed with 766/792. The serial run solved more tests and had a cleaner single-owner build path, while the parallel run incurred a concrete shared-workspace overwrite/reconciliation episode. Because both failed, the retained pattern is an adverse parallel process difference and not an outcome-differential root cause.
parallel_contributors: Parallel agents wrote deliverable-level source and build files in one shared workspace, producing changed compile.sh, overlapping Go files, unexpected Rust files, and cleanup before delivery.
serial_contributors: Serial kept one coherent Go source and compile path, including the explicit removal of the original executable before a successful rebuild.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both attempts had residual behavioral incompatibilities under official tests; serial's final implementation passed 17 more tests than parallel.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; supported process contrast only
